sections.label: Building bonds between communities
sections.summary: Efforts aim to build bonds and understanding between people and communities so discrimination can be minimised, with IRCCs letting community leaders build friendships and speak up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The focus of all our efforts, through our various initiatives and programmes, is to build bonds and understanding between people and communities, so that discrimination can be minimised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For example, the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs) allow community leaders to build friendships and speak up when they see fellow Singaporeans being discriminated against across ethnic and religious lines.

sections.label: Racial, religious and gender equality surveys
sections.summary: A 2013 OnePeople.SG and IPS survey showed eight in 10 respondents comfortable with a close friend of another race or religion, and the UN ranked Singapore 13th of 155 on gender inequality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For instance, as an indication of the state of racial and religious harmony, a survey by OnePeople.SG and the Institute of Policy Studies in 2013 showed that eight out of 10 respondents were comfortable having a close friend from another race or religion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As a measure of the state of our gender equality, the UN's 2015 Human Development Report ranked Singapore 13th out of 155 countries on the Gender Inequality Index, which means that we are good, right up there in the top percentile – the lower the ranking, the higher you are – we are more equal.

sections.label: MCCY support on workplace discrimination
sections.summary: MCCY supports efforts to address discrimination in areas covered by other Ministries and agencies such as MOM and TAFEP, and IRCC and IRO conferences of 200-300 discussed racial and religious issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And, lastly, how does MCCY support efforts to address discrimination in areas covered by other Ministries and Government agencies, such as MOM and TAFEP, to understand and deal with workplace discrimination?

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Also, in IRCCs and IRO, we have held conferences as large as 200-300 strong to discuss issues confronting us on racial and religious lines.

sections.label: National Integration Council and fault-lines
sections.summary: MOM leads the National Integration Council's sectoral discussion on the workplace, and as a young nation Singapore has fault-lines along race, making nation-building and social cohesion ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: For example, on the National Integration Council, we have MOM leading the sectoral discussion on the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In short, this is a very important question for us because, as a very young nation, we do have our natural fault-lines along race and racial perspectives but also, increasingly, we have new fault-lines, new forces that are pulling us apart.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And even more established societies are finding themselves being pulled in many directions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, nation-building, social cohesion are an ongoing process.
